title: Hybrid Rice Breakthrough
summary: In 1970 Yuan Longping's team in China found a male-sterile wild rice, which became the basis of a three-line hybrid breeding system. The first hybrid rice with strong heterosis was created in 1973, and mass cultivation had begun by 1976.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on 1973 for the first strong-heterosis three-line hybrid; the 1970 discovery and 1976 mass cultivation are given as separate dates.

as_recorded.value: a successful three-line hybrid rice breeding system in 1973

where.modern_name: Yazhou District, Sanya, Hainan, China (district-level pin; the CUHK page places the work in the former Yaxian County)

importance.justification: Asian Scientist says a fifth of all rice grown worldwide now comes from the hybrid rice first cultivated by Yuan.

sources.title: China’s Father Of Hybrid Rice, Yuan Longping, Passes At 90 (In Memoriam)

reviewer_note: Coordinator review 2026-11-03: summary confirmed on the CUHK bulletin (OCR text) and Asian Scientist. Replaced a GeoNames search page with an OpenStreetMap district point. The CUHK page dates the male-sterile wild rice to November 1970 and the first strongly heterotic hybrid to 1973; Asian Scientist is a magazine, so CUHK is the institutional source.
